chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Fadhl and Al-Hajjāl from Tha'labah from Abu Khalid Al-Qammāt from Abd al-Khāliq Al-Ṣayqālī who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And whoever enters it is safe.' He said, 'You have asked me about something no one has asked me about, except whom Allah wills.'

Then he said, 'Whoever leads to this House (Kaaba) while knowing that it is the House that Allah commanded, and knows us, the People of the House, with true knowledge of us, will be safe in this world and the Hereafter.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for true safety in the Kaaba according to the Imam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the concept of 'safety' (amn) from mere physical protection within the Kaaba to a spiritual security in both the dunya and akhira, contingent upon 'haqq al-ma'rifa' (true knowledge) of the Ahl al-Bayt. This interpretation underscores the Shia theological principle that correct belief in the divine authority of the Imams is the essential key to the spiritual benefits of acts of worship, such as Hajj.
